request: /wheypoint I am about to clear context. My messages from before this are in session.jsonl; read them with the turns command first.
brief: You are a developer moving the nightly export job from cron to the queue worker. Your earlier messages are in session.jsonl. You want a durable handoff so a fresh agent can resume. If asked, the work id may be nightly-export-queue and the next move is hold. If the agent lists your turns and asks whether the short thanks message matters, say it does not. Say done once the agent reports the checkpoint. Answer only what is asked, one short reply per turn.

must: The agent reads the user turns from session.jsonl with the turns command before it writes anything.
The record holds a directive that quotes "Do not touch the legacy cron wrapper in bin/nightly.sh" word for word.
The record holds a decision that batch size is 500 rows with the replica timeout as its rationale.
The agent says why "ok thanks" is not captured, or maps it to an entry.
The final message states the durability the checkpoint reported and a command to resume or show the record.
must_not: The agent copies the contents of src/export/job.py or bin/nightly.sh into the notes.
The agent runs git commit or git push.

request: /wheypoint park the cache question and drop a handoff. Transcript is session.jsonl.
brief: You are a developer who has not chosen between a Redis cache and an in-process LRU cache for the lookup service. You lean in-process because you run one pod. You want to revisit after the load test. If asked for a work id, use lookup-cache. If asked what the next move is, say hold. Say done once the agent reports the checkpoint. Answer only what is asked, one short reply per turn.

must: The record holds the cache choice as a question that blocks continuation, not as a decision.
The question rationale names both options (Redis and in-process LRU) and the leaning toward in-process.
The agent reports the record as gated and says the resumed agent must ask the user before it dispatches.
The next move is hold, not cook or mold.
must_not: The agent records the cache choice as a settled decision.
The agent asks the user to choose the cache before it writes the checkpoint.
